title: The 10 Best Cordless Finish Nailers
subtitle: Battery-powered 15- and 16-gauge finish nailers for trim with no compressor or hose, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A cordless finish nailer drives 15 or 16-gauge trim nails with no compressor, hose or gas cartridge, which makes punch-list and single-room trim jobs far quicker to set up. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (a brushless motor, switchable sequential and bump fire, a battery in the box and a 3-year-plus warranty). Expect 6 to 9 lbs, heavier than an air nailer. They run from about $171 for RYOBI's P326 to $395 for Metabo HPT's 15-gauge kit.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

avoid.name: Ecarke Finish Nailer 16 Gauge Compatible with Dewalt 20V Battery, Cordless Straight Brad Nailer
avoid.flag: Rated 2.3; heavier than the DEWALT it imitates
avoid.verdict: A DEWALT-battery clone that costs more than RYOBI's real nailer and rates far worse. If you're on DEWALT batteries, save for the DCN662B or DCN660B.
reasons: It's rated 2.2 stars, far below every nailer we rank (4.2 and up).
At 8.95 lbs it's nearly 3 lbs heavier than the DEWALT DCN662B it's built to run alongside, and its title calls it both a finish nailer and a 'brad nailer'.
It's a third-party body on DEWALT batteries, so DEWALT doesn't warrant it, and the listing names no warranty of its own.

buyers_guide.a: Cordless nailers skip the compressor and hose, which saves setup time on small jobs and punch lists. They're heavier (6 to 9 lbs vs 4 lbs) and cost more. For all-day production trim, an air nailer is lighter and cheaper.
Angled magazines reach into corners and under cabinets more easily, and most 15-gauge nailers are angled. Straight 16-gauge nails cost less.

buyers_guide.q: Do cordless nailers have a delay?
buyers_guide.a: Some flywheel designs spin up for a moment before firing. Air-spring designs like Metabo HPT's fire immediately, closer to a pneumatic nailer.
Makers quote 375 to 800 nails per charge on a 2.0Ah battery, depending on the tool and the wood. A spare battery covers a full day of trim.

buyers_guide.q: Can a finish nailer do framing?
buyers_guide.a: No. Finish nailers drive 15 or 16-gauge nails for trim. Framing, sheathing and subfloor need a framing nailer with 2- to 3-1/2-inch clipped or round-head nails.
